name: Viking ROADS randomly assigned 574 eligible SUNY Westchester students to program eligibility or usual services.
description: The study enrolled 288 program-group and 286 control-group students across fall 2019, fall 2020, and spring 2021. Controls could use existing college services but were not eligible for Viking ROADS.

values.value: Randomized controlled trial; 288 program and 286 control students.

context: Viking ROADS three-year randomized evaluation at SUNY Westchester; outcome horizons and the COVID-era setting remain explicit.
name: Viking ROADS increased SUNY Westchester enrollment in semester 3 by 8.2 percentage points (73.9% versus 65.8%).
description: This is a semester-3 enrollment result within a six-semester follow-up. It does not measure degree completion or enrollment at every college.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in SUNY Westchester enrollment in semester 3, program minus control.

context: Viking ROADS three-year randomized evaluation at SUNY Westchester; outcome horizons and the COVID-era setting remain explicit.
name: Viking ROADS students had 3.6 more cumulative credits by the end of semester 3.
description: The source reports this three-semester credit-attainment difference during the randomized follow-up. It is not a cost, degree, or later labor-market estimate.

values.value: Difference in cumulative credits earned by end of semester 3, program minus control.

name: Viking ROADS increased credential attainment by 11.8 percentage points after six semesters (35.5% versus 23.7%).
description: The confirmatory three-year outcome is any degree or certificate at any college. The study was conducted at one college during major COVID-era disruptions.

values.value: Percentage-point difference in any degree or certificate attainment at any college after six semesters, program minus control.

description: The report cites this as a three-year threshold result and discusses it alongside the larger credential-attainment difference. It is not a complete explanation of the program’s mechanism.
